Team Code Blooded · Flame in Freefall

Which fire tests can we compare?

FIRST FIRE helps aerospace researchers and engineering students decide which NASA flight records support a fire-safety question.

Follow two decisions about burning droplets and smoke detectors. In each, a single recorded condition changes what the evidence can support.

FLEX · NASA PSI-69

Does more oxygen extend the burn?

Compare methanol droplets at 15% and 21% chamber oxygen and a target pressure of 14.7 psia. Match the starting conditions before revealing burn durations.

+1.6 s

Mean across three pairs. The higher-oxygen droplet burned for less time in two of them.

FLEX · Sensitivity to the matching rule

The answer changes with the match.

Eligibility rulePairsMean change
≤ 0.35 mm apart3+1.6 s
≤ 0.05 mm apart1−3.3 s
Also require same UTC day0Unavailable

A closer diameter match reverses the sign. A same-day rule leaves no pair to compare.

The next test would run both oxygen settings on the same day with closely matched droplets and the same definition of burn duration.

SAME-R · NASA PSI-101

Three smoke runs produced different signals.

Kapton runs 75, 85 and 93 used the same nominal inlet speed, heater setting and heating duration.

Run 85 had the largest optical drop in the first five minutes, reaching 1.031 V at 164 seconds. An optical signal and an alarm flag are separate measurements.

Was the Shuttle detector powered?

0 / 3,792

Shuttle power-on records in the three repeat runs. Their silent alarm channel cannot establish three missed alarms.

Run 92 confirms that the power flag can turn on. Its heater setting differed. Detector readiness and matched smoke exposure would still need checking.

Independent replay · Science education

Let another lab check the decision.

Share the experiment

Export the FLEX study JSON or copy its comparison link. A second lab can check the same record IDs, settings and result, then propose a matched follow-up.

Try it in a classroom

Students in Amaravati or elsewhere can compare two NIST room experiments in English or Telugu. The exercise asks students to match a reported alarm reading to its timestamp on the instrument trace.

The revised archive calculator passed 22 of 24 new questions on its first attempt. Human study outcomes, classroom adoption and independent researcher sign-off remain unmeasured.
